title: Prior-to-posterior contraction and effective likelihood rank measure information, not bias
question: CMP-14 asks for two default summaries, prior-to-posterior contraction per interaction and an effective likelihood rank, so an analyst sees when an aggregate-only interaction is held up by its prior. Would those summaries tell the analyst whether the reported interval covers?
answer: Not reliably, and the reason is structural. On an exact identity-link arm of 504 scenarios and a logit arm of 72, no threshold on contraction, on either effective-rank reading, or on the estimability screen separates scenarios whose 95% interval covers nominally from those that fail. The summaries are functions of Fisher information and the prior, so within one design they are exactly constant while coverage ranges from 0 to 0.96. They partly catch the failure they were designed for: contraction flags 59% of failures caused by a tight prior. They catch none of the 142 failures caused by a biased route, where the ecological route carries between-study confounding or the additivity route a synergy, because confounding moves the posterior mean and not its information. A clean contraction says the likelihood spoke, not that it was right. Every result is exploratory.
findings: All four registered statistics (contraction, target-level likelihood ratio, whole-model effective rank, estimability screen) take values shared by failing and nominal scenarios on both arms, so no threshold on any of them separates the classes. On E1 there are 251 failing and 169 nominal scenarios; on E2, 41 and 12.

On the identity link with known residual variance the posterior covariance does not involve the outcomes. Within one information state, spread, network size and prior, contraction, target ratio and effective rank are exactly constant across discordance and synergy levels while coverage ranges over 0.956.

Decomposed by cause (post hoc), 109 E1 failures come from a prior of SD 0.1 pulling a true interaction of 0.4 toward zero and 142 from a biased route. Contraction flags 58.7% of the first and 0% of the second; target ratio 41.3% and 0%; effective rank 56.0% and 0%.
Scenario pairs matched on spread, size and prior whose contraction differs by less than 0.02 differ in coverage by up to 0.951 on E1.

On the logit arm the rules score far better on average (contraction Youden 0.805 against 0.220 on E1) because 34 of its 41 failures sit at the tight prior and it has only 12 nominal scenarios. The overlap persists.

Three aggregate routes identify an interaction on the logit link, through differences in covariate means, covariate variances or baseline risk; only the first works on the identity link. None is randomized.
not_answered: Nothing here is confirmatory: E1 was computed before its protocol existed, E2's separation rules were rebuilt after its output was read, and the cause decomposition was added for the manuscript. E1 is exact for a design realized at its quadrature nodes and E2 is asymptotic, so no posterior was sampled and neither is an average over realized designs. The exact invariance of the summaries holds for known-variance Gaussian models; with estimated variances or random effects they would move with a departure and whether that movement could ever warn is untested. One target component, one covariate, one network geometry, a normal within-study covariate law on the logit arm, and departures acting on the mean only. The protocol went through thirteen rounds of critique; the manuscript has not been peer reviewed.
design: Exact computation on a four-component network, one scalar covariate, twelve arms in every state. The target interaction is identified by its own IPD trial, by a combination arm under additivity, by the between-study contrast in aggregate covariate means, by differing covariate variances (logit only), or not at all. E1: identity link, known variance, 504 scenarios crossing state, covariate spread, network size, interaction prior SD, discordance and synergy. E2: logit link, asymptotic, 72 scenarios.
estimand: The within-trial interaction of the target component, true value 0.4; coverage of its nominal 95% interval
methods_compared: target-level likelihood to prior precision ratio
n_sim: Exact and asymptotic computation: 504 E1 scenarios and 72 E2 scenarios, no Monte Carlo replicates
